resolved_by: The 2004 amendment to Fed. R. Crim. P. 35, which replaced "imposition of sentence" with "sentencing" and added Rule 35(c), defining sentencing as oral announcement of the sentence
issue: For purposes of 18 U.S.C. § 3582(c) and Rule 35, is a sentence imposed when it is orally pronounced at the sentencing hearing, or when the written judgment is entered?

sides.position: A sentence is imposed when it is orally pronounced at the sentencing hearing (the sizable majority view before the 2004 amendment)
cases: United States v. Aguirre, 214 F.3d 1122 (9th Cir. 2000)
United States v. Melvin, 105 F.4th 620 (4th Cir. 2024)

sides.position: A sentence is imposed only when the written judgment is entered (the minority view before the 2004 amendment)
cases: United States v. Aguirre, 214 F.3d 1122 (9th Cir. 2000)

this_court: Takes the oral-pronouncement view: a sentence is not imposed until it has been unequivocally pronounced during the sentencing hearing
quote: The circuits were divided, with a sizable majority holding that Rule 35 refers to the sentencing hearing, and a minority holding that the clock starts only when written judgment is entered.
cite: United States v. Gilbert Melvin, 105 F.4th 620 (4th Cir. 2024)
